definition: A queue with an explicit capacity or admission limit. It bounds memory and waiting exposure; it does not increase the service rate or eliminate overload.
Making a derived cached value unusable after a change. An invalidation can race with an older fill, so ordering and version checks matter.
A request to stop work that is no longer needed. Each stage must cooperate and release resources; a committed external effect may still need reconciliation.
Checking the peer’s certificate and the expected service identity under a trust policy. Encryption without authenticating the intended endpoint does not establish who receives the plaintext.
A load model in which each simulated user waits before issuing its next request. It can represent real interaction, but slower responses may reduce offered load.
Stopping new work while allowing bounded in-flight work to finish before closing a process or connection. Long-lived clients need an explicit reconnect and recovery plan.
The dependent chain of work that determines completion time. Independent branches can overlap; sequential dependencies accumulate.
Pagination using a stable ordering position instead of only a numeric offset. Define tie-breakers, mutation behavior, expiry, and authorization of the cursor.
Feedback tied to actual submitted work, concrete excerpts, and an explicit rubric. A total score is derived from recorded dimensions and is not a hiring guarantee.
Progress waits for earlier required work. TCP byte ordering can hold later bytes behind a gap; an HTTP/2 application stream and a transport byte stream have different ordering boundaries.
A logical request/response channel multiplexed within an HTTP/2 connection. Independent streams still share transport behavior and resource limits.
An operation whose intended effect is the same when applied repeatedly with the same meaning. This does not promise identical responses or make all surrounding side effects safe.
Assignment based on transport/network information, often at connection or flow granularity. Equal connection counts do not imply equal request cost.
Routing using application information such as an HTTP hostname or path. Access to encrypted application data generally requires an appropriate TLS termination boundary.

For a stable system with consistent boundaries, average work in progress equals average throughput times average time in the system: L = λW. Use matching units and do not treat an unstable, growing backlog as steady state.
A measurable quality or constraint: latency, availability, durability, privacy, cost, or an operational limit. “Fast” becomes useful only after defining a workload and threshold.
A load model that schedules arrivals independently of prior completions, within generator capacity. It can expose backlog growth that a waiting-client loop may suppress.
A stated multiplier from an average arrival rate to a modeled busy interval. It is an assumption to validate, not a universal constant for all products.

A boundary in an ordered sample distribution. A p95 below 200 ms describes approximately 95% of the measured population under the chosen convention; it does not bound every request. Do not average instance percentiles into a fleet percentile.
A schema-based encoding and interface toolchain. Field numbers carry wire identity, so contract evolution must preserve their meaning and avoid recycling removed numbers.
An ordered byte stream within a QUIC connection. Loss affecting one stream’s data need not block delivery of unrelated stream data, though congestion and shared resource limits still matter.
A stable position identifying the history already applied by a client. Recovery requires retained history or a defined snapshot fallback and fresh authorization.

Remote procedure call: an interface shaped as an operation on another process. Generated bindings reduce encoding work; they do not remove network delays, uncertain outcomes, or authorization requirements.
A method whose defined semantics are essentially read-only. Safety and idempotence are distinct properties; neither is a claim that a broken implementation cannot mutate state.
A learner’s own evaluation of submitted reasoning against a rubric. This academy labels it separately from objective quiz results and model-generated feedback.
A server-to-client event stream over HTTP. Reconnect metadata can help resume delivery, but the application must supply retention and replay semantics.
An explicit model used to explore consequences under stated assumptions. Its generated output is illustrative and must not be presented as measured production performance.
A value that does not include some newer authoritative update. Whether serving it is acceptable depends on the operation’s freshness and correctness contract.
The endpoint that decrypts a TLS connection. Plaintext is available there, so its identity, access, logging, and any next network hop belong in the trust model.
A set of explicit assumptions about users, arrival rates, request mix, object sizes, skew, and growth. Estimates should expose the assumptions that could change the architecture.
